slides.headline: She leads a global fight against violence toward women. In 2026, she became only the second South Asian in the National Women's Hall of Fame.
Mona Sinha was inducted into the National Women's Hall of Fame on September 24, 2026
slides.body: The ceremony, held at the George Eastman Museum in Rochester, NY, recognized more than 40 years of her leadership in gender equality, philanthropy and advocacy. She is only the second South Asian ever inducted, after Indra Nooyi - joining a roster that includes Michelle Obama, Rosa Parks and Janet Yellen.

slides.headline: As CEO of Equality Now, her work secured 17 legal changes across nine countries in 2025 alone.
slides.body: Those legal reforms against discrimination and violence toward women and girls are estimated to have benefited 69 million women and girls - concrete policy change, not symbolic advocacy.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs its diaspora shaping global rules, not just global companies.
slides.body: Sinha's induction marks an Indian-origin leader influencing international law on women's rights at the highest level - a different kind of global Indian success story than the ones usually celebrated.
